findings.summary: This is not a regression. Once an accepted accessory step has held through a full cadence period, the next calendar turn may move the slot to a lower-skill alternative that is not on the chain. Example: pull-up -> band-pulldown at week 13 under COACH_DECIDES and EVERY_6_WEEKS. This matches the revised rule (only rungs below on the chain are excluded) and the catalog's rotation, which allows skill(B) <= skill(A). Recorded so that the Q-R7B-01 resolution is not read as 'a reached configuration is permanent'.

Residual wording in MOVEMENT_PATTERN_UNAVAILABLE. For a novice with bands and a bar it says 'No available equipment supports PUSH' while TPL.UPPER already prescribes incline-push-up. The gap is the second (accessory) PUSH slot. The option is now correct and effective, so only the wording is pattern-level rather than slot-level. Owner: next runtime or copy revision.

One SSCTR matter was seen in passing but is not part of this delta: an EASY_LOW athlete with a 10K race is not graduated in 16 weeks, because each block's last week is a consolidation week planned below the 60-minute evidence threshold. The block reviews disclose this truthfully as RUN_QUALITY_NOT_YET with the reasons (recheck/out/p09d-easylow-race.json). Whether the evidence window should skip consolidation weeks is for SSCTR.
